name: Prone T Leg Abduction
summary: A bodyweight posterior-chain exercise performed lying prone in a T-position while isometrically holding back extension and actively opening and closing the legs.

setup: Lie face down on the floor or an exercise mat with your legs straight and spread wider than shoulder-width.
Extend your arms straight out to the sides perpendicular to your torso to form a T-shape.
Rotate your hands so your thumbs point toward the ceiling.
steps: Engage your glutes, back, and rear shoulders to lift your chest, arms, and thighs off the floor.
Hold this elevated isometric extension throughout the set.
Smoothly bring your legs together until your feet touch or nearly touch.
Spread your legs back out to the starting wide position while keeping the thighs elevated.
Repeat the leg opening and closing motion for the desired number of repetitions while maintaining torso elevation.
instructions.breathing: Breathe continuously and rhythmically throughout the movement, avoiding holding your breath against the abdominal pressure.

common_faults.fault: Hyperextending the cervical spine by craning the neck upward.
common_faults.correction: Keep your gaze directed toward the floor to maintain a neutral cervical alignment.

common_faults.fault: Allowing the thighs or chest to drop to the floor during leg movement.
common_faults.correction: Actively contract the glutes and upper back to keep limbs elevated throughout the entire set.

common_faults.fault: Bending the knees to move the legs instead of driving through the hips.
common_faults.correction: Keep your knees fully extended and focus on hip abduction and adduction.

precautions: Individuals with acute lower back sensitivity should limit the height of trunk extension.
